A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same position paper. Their complete text, seven figures, mathematical notation, references, and Appendix A support comparison despite reflow and added discussion.

before.justification: Appendix A.1 reports original validation of a GPT-4o paper classifier on 200 sampled papers, achieving 92% recall. The paper also reports illustrative model outputs with prompts in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: V2 retains the original 200-paper classifier validation and its 92% recall, together with the illustrative model outputs and appendix prompts.

M1.justification: The Constructed Response and Explanation MCQA formats retain the same procedures. Recommendations involving rubrics, calibrated scoring, IRT, and adversarial collection are also retained; the multilingual discussion elaborates their application without specifying a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The paper-screening validation and illustrative MCQA scenarios remain unchanged. V2 discusses multilingual construction and cites additional benchmarks without conducting evaluations on new datasets, languages, or tasks.

E2.justification: No comparison method is added to or removed from the original validation or model illustrations. Additional cited methods are discussed as related work rather than evaluated as new baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 retains the same screening procedure, relevance categories, corpus counts, and 200-paper validation sample. Appendix A.2 retains the same prompts; no changed evaluation metric, control, or testing procedure is reported.

E4.justification: The rubric-checking, obscure/adversarial MCQ, and symbol/order/explanation examples in Figures 4, 6, and 7 remain unchanged. The added multilingual and feasibility discussions introduce no new ablation, robustness test, or empirical case study.

E5.justification: Both versions report the classifier's point estimate without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: The original outcomes remain unchanged, including 92% classifier recall, 42% filtering, the 122-paper initial reading list, and the illustrated model answers. Section 3.2 also retains the same MCQA prevalence percentages and 7.2% validation-query estimate.

T1.justification: The basic MCQA and generative-format definitions are unchanged, as is the qualitative account of IRT. V2 introduces no new or revised formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 7 retain the central position: reform MCQA through educational testing practices and generative alternatives while preserving its useful roles. The added arguments do not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 adds limitations of native-language collection and translation when constructing multilingual MCQs. Section 8 adds a response to generative evaluation's implementation costs using historical analogies. Section 6.3 also changes its explanation of misleading outputs from prioritizing preferences over accuracy to preferences over helpfulness.

D1.justification: The search and screening details in Appendix A.1 and all twelve prompts in Appendix A.2 are retained. No new implementation settings, hardware information, or code/data access instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds references on automated question assessment, justification scoring, multilingual evaluation, and historical evaluation shifts while retaining its educational-testing perspective. Some sources are replaced: Section 5.4.2 substitutes Wallace et al. (2019), listed as a question-answering paper, for Eisenschlos et al. (2021) when discussing fact-checking. Publication updates elsewhere concern the same works.

P1.justification: V2 makes local prose and terminology edits, expands Sections 4.2, 6.2, and 8, and revises and moves the acknowledgments before the limitations. The main section hierarchy and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All seven figures remain. Figures 5 and 6 change their paired examples from side-by-side to stacked boxes, Figure 3 changes its in-figure labels to Explanation, and Figure 7 receives spacing and caption edits. The surrounding text reflows within the retained two-column layout.

improvement.justification: The multilingual construction caveats in Section 6.2 and the fuller response to implementation costs in Section 8 modestly strengthen the paper's practical guidance and argument. The stacked diagrams also improve readability. These gains outweigh the localized concern about the less clearly matched fact-checking citation in Section 5.4.2; the underlying empirical support remains unchanged.
